record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.context_brief: Pattern properties invariant under tiling equivalence
record.original_question: Identify and classify tilings that possess some strengthened geometric pattern property—motivated by properties such as bounded displacement equivalence, bi-Lipschitz equivalence, linear repetitivity, or similar notions—with the feature that every tiling mutually locally derivable from it, topologically conjugate to it, or homeomorphic to it also has that same property.

evidence.quote: A natural question is thus to ask whether one can reconcile the two approaches. One strategy to answer this question is to consider a strong version of the BD or BL or LR or ... properties. Problem 2.7.1 Classify tilings with such a property that any other tiling MLD (or topologically conjugate, or homeomorphic) to it also has that property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by polytopal tiles drawn from a finite set of prototiles up to translation. Two tilings $\mathcal{T}_1,\mathcal{T}_2$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ are said to be:

(a) Mutually locally derivable (MLD) if there exists $R>0$ such that for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the patch of $\mathcal{T}_2$ inside the ball $B(x,1)$ is determined by the patch of $\mathcal{T}_1$ inside $B(x,R)$, and vice versa.

(b) Topologically conjugate if their associated tiling dynamical systems (the orbit closures in the local-topology hull under the $\mathbb{R}^d$-translation action) are conjugate as topological dynamical systems.

(c) Homeomorphic if their hulls are homeomorphic as topological spaces.

A pattern property $P$ for tilings is, for instance, one of the following:

• Bounded displacement (BD) equivalence to a lattice: there exists a bijection $\phi$ from the set of tile-centers of $\mathcal{T}$ to a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\sup_x \|\phi(x)-x\|<\infty$.

• Bi-Lipschitz (BL) equivalence to a lattice: such a bijection $\phi$ exists which is bi-Lipschitz when extended appropriately.

• Linear repetitivity (LR): there exists $C>0$ such that every patch of $\mathcal{T}$ of diameter $r$ that occurs in $\mathcal{T}$ already occurs in every ball of radius $Cr$.

Problem. For each such pattern property $P$ (and for analogous strengthened variants), determine and classify all tilings $\mathcal{T}$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the following invariance feature: every tiling $\mathcal{T}'$ that is MLD to $\mathcal{T}$ (respectively, topologically conjugate to $\mathcal{T}$, respectively, homeomorphic to $\mathcal{T}$ in the hull sense) also satisfies property $P$. In other words, characterize those tilings for which property $P$ is preserved under the chosen equivalence relation, and identify a strengthening of $P$ that is automatically invariant under MLD equivalence, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism of hulls.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open classification/research problem on identifying invariant strengthenings of bounded-displacement, bi-Lipschitz, and linear-repetitivity properties under MLD, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism. No comprehensive classification has been located in the literature; partial results exist for linear repetitivity (which is known to be MLD-invariant and has connections with topological conjugacy results due to Aliste-Prieto, Coronel, Gambaudo, and others), while BD/BL invariance is more subtle. Overall the problem remains open in its general classification form.

status_evidence.title: Linearly repetitive Delone sets are rectifiable
status_evidence.snippet: Aliste-Prieto, Coronel, Gambaudo show LR Delone sets are bounded-displacement equivalent to a lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist relating LR to BD equivalence, but a general classification under MLD/topological conjugacy/homeomorphism is not established.
